chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from some of our companions, from Sa'id al-A'raj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
A man should not shave (take hair) when he sees the crescent of Dhi al-Qa'dah, whether he intends to remove it from his head or from his beard.

key_terms.الْخُرُوجَ: Removal (of hair), specifically referring to shaving or cutting
key_terms.ذِي الْقَعْدَةِ: Dhi al-Qa'dah, the eleventh month of the Islamic lunar calendar
key_terms.هِلَالُ: The crescent moon, marking the beginning of a lunar month

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on shaving hair during the first days of Dhi al-Qa'dah according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) prescribes refraining from shaving the head or beard upon sighting the Dhi al-Qa'dah crescent, a practice rooted in the tradition of the Imams to mark the beginning of the month with distinct physical preparation. This act serves as a tangible spiritual discipline, aligning personal grooming with the sacred rhythm of the lunar calendar and demonstrating reverence for the holy months.
